title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Use this guide when the CaviWave Pro is completely unresponsive, starts incompletely, or does not reach its normal ready condition.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Safety and Processing Continuity
steps.instructions: Remove the ultrasonic cleaner from processing use if it cannot reliably power on or complete startup. Do not place instruments into a unit whose operating state cannot be confirmed. Move instrument processing to another validated cleaning method or available unit according to department procedure. Expected outcome: Processing continues on verified equipment while the affected cleaner is evaluated safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Ask staff what occurred and reproduce the problem without a load when safe. Determine whether the system is completely dead, briefly powers and shuts down, freezes during startup, or displays an alarm or message. Record any visible indicators or messages exactly rather than paraphrasing them. Expected outcome: The failure mode is clearly identified and repeatable, or the device starts normally and the original complaint can be investigated as intermittent.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Power
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord, plug, receptacle, disconnect, and any accessible facility power controls associated with the cleaner. Check for obvious damage, looseness, heat discoloration, or a partially disconnected plug. Verify the receptacle or supplied branch power using an appropriate approved method. Do not repeatedly reset a breaker or disconnect that will not remain set. Expected outcome: Stable facility power is confirmed at the unit. If restoring an external power connection corrects startup and the system operates normally, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Power Connections and Controls
steps.instructions: Verify that the main power control is in the correct operating position and that accessible cords or connectors have not been pulled loose during cleaning, movement, or service activity. Look for liquid intrusion, damaged insulation, burnt odor, unusual heat, or visible physical damage. Expected outcome: External power connections are secure and no unsafe condition is present. Any sign of overheating, liquid intrusion, or electrical damage requires removal from service.

steps.title: 5. Check Emergency Stops or External Interlocks if Equipped
steps.instructions: Inspect any externally accessible emergency-stop, safety switch, lid/door position, or similar interlock that can inhibit startup or operation. Do not bypass or defeat an interlock. Expected outcome: All external safety controls are in their normal operating state. If correcting an external interlock condition restores normal startup, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Remove Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect only nonessential external peripherals that can be safely removed, such as optional data connections or tracking accessories, then attempt a normal startup. Do not disconnect plumbing, protective grounding, or required safety devices merely to force startup. Expected outcome: The system completes startup with required connections intact. If one optional peripheral consistently prevents startup, leave that peripheral disconnected only if permitted and escalate the accessory separately.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Power Cycle
steps.instructions: With the unit unloaded and not in clinical processing use, shut it down using the normal control method. Allow the system to fully power down, then restart it once. Avoid repeated rapid cycling. Expected outcome: The cleaner progresses through startup and reaches its normal ready state without freezing, resetting, or alarming. If successful, continue to functional verification.

steps.title: 8. Observe Startup Behavior
steps.instructions: Watch the display, indicators, pumps, valves, and other externally observable startup activity. Note the exact point where startup stops or repeats. Do not enter restricted service modes or alter protected configuration settings. Expected outcome: Startup either completes normally or a consistent failure point is documented for escalation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Once the system starts normally, verify that the user interface responds, the chamber is empty and safe, no abnormal leaks or noises are present, and an appropriate unloaded or department-approved functional check can be completed. Expected outcome: The unit starts consistently and basic operation is normal. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If verified power is present but the cleaner remains dead, resets, freezes, or cannot complete startup, stop external troubleshooting. Do not proceed into internal power supplies, control boards, wiring assemblies, or protected service functions without approved service documentation and authorization. Expected outcome: The device remains removed from service and is routed for qualified bench or manufacturer-level evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the CaviWave Pro would not power on at the beginning of the shift.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the unit's external power connection was loose and facility power at the receptacle was otherwise normal.
CCR.Resolution: Secured the power connection, restarted the cleaner, verified normal startup and basic operation, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the issue followed cleaning, movement, or outage
Unusual odor, heat, sound, or visible damage
Results before and after power cycle

title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - Cycle Will Not Start, Aborts, or Stalls
description: Use this guide when a cleaning cycle will not begin, stops unexpectedly, repeatedly aborts, or remains stuck in one part of the process.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not rely on an interrupted or incomplete cycle as a completed cleaning process. Remove affected instruments from the workflow and reprocess them according to department policy using verified equipment. Expected outcome: No load is released based on an incomplete or uncertain cleaning cycle.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Cycle Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the cycle fails before starting, aborts shortly after initiation, stalls during filling, heating, ultrasonic operation, draining, or another visible phase. Record any displayed message and the approximate point in the cycle where the failure occurs. Expected outcome: The failure is tied to a specific part of the cycle rather than being recorded only as "cycle failed."

steps.title: 3. Verify the Chamber and Lid/Door Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm that the chamber is not overloaded and that racks, baskets, instruments, or tubing are not interfering with closure or any accessible safety interlock. Inspect the lid or door for obvious obstruction, damage, or misalignment. Expected outcome: The chamber is loaded appropriately and the closure mechanism reaches its normal operating position. If correcting an obstruction allows the cycle to run normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Water and Drain Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that required incoming water services are available and that accessible supply valves are open. Inspect the drain path for obvious external restrictions, kinked hoses, standing water, or facility drainage problems. Expected outcome: Water supply and drainage are available. If restoring an external utility resolves the cycle failure, verify a successful cycle and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Verify Detergent or Chemistry Availability
steps.instructions: Check the installed chemistry container, pickup tubing, and accessible connections for empty supply, incorrect placement, kinks, loose fittings, or obvious air entry where visible. Use only the approved chemistry and handling practices specified for the department and equipment. Expected outcome: Chemistry is available and correctly connected. A corrected external chemistry problem should allow normal cycle progression.

steps.title: 6. Review Operator-Selectable Cycle Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm that staff selected the intended cycle and that no obvious operator-accessible configuration or cycle selection is preventing operation. Do not alter protected service parameters or undocumented settings. Expected outcome: The intended cycle is selected with normal user-accessible settings.

steps.title: 7. Inspect External Sensors and Interlocks
steps.instructions: Where accessible, inspect lid/door position hardware, level-related external connections, and other visible interlock components for contamination, obstruction, or damage. Do not defeat an interlock to make the cycle continue. Expected outcome: No external condition is falsely preventing cycle progression.

steps.title: 8. Attempt a Controlled Unloaded Cycle
steps.instructions: If safe and permitted by department procedure, run an appropriate unloaded cycle after correcting external issues. Observe whether the cycle fills, heats, operates, drains, and completes normally. Expected outcome: The cycle completes without abnormal delay, abort, or stall. If successful, the issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Compare Repeated Failures
steps.instructions: If the cycle fails again, determine whether it stops at the same point each time. Consistency can help separate utility, interlock, chemistry, drainage, temperature, and internal-control categories. Do not repeatedly run failed cycles merely to force completion. Expected outcome: A repeatable failure point is documented for service escalation.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Cycling Is Unreliable
steps.instructions: If the unit cannot complete a normal cycle reliably after external causes are ruled out, remove it from service. Expected outcome: Instruments are not processed through equipment with unreliable cleaning-cycle completion.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the CaviWave Pro repeatedly stopped during the fill portion of the cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the incoming water supply valve to the unit was partially closed.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the water supply valve to its normal operating position, completed an unloaded functional cycle successfully, and returned the cleaner to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the failure repeats at the same phase

title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - Door Will Not Lock, Unlock, or Seal
description: Use this guide when the lid or door will not close, latch, release, or maintain the condition required for normal cycle operation.

steps.title: 1. Protect Personnel and Processing Safety
steps.instructions: Do not force the lid or door, defeat a latch, or begin a cycle if the closure cannot be confirmed. If a cycle has stopped with liquid or instruments inside, follow approved department and manufacturer procedures before attempting access. Expected outcome: Personnel are protected from hot liquid, chemistry, or unintended equipment operation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Closure Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the door will not physically close, closes but is not recognized, will not lock, unexpectedly releases, leaks around the seal, or remains locked after the cycle. Expected outcome: The mechanical or recognition symptom is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Physical Obstructions
steps.instructions: Check baskets, instruments, racks, tubing, labels, debris, and other items around the opening and closure path. Remove only obvious external obstructions. Expected outcome: The lid or door moves freely through its normal external range. If removing an obstruction restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Seal and Mating Surface
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the accessible seal and surrounding contact surface for contamination, displaced material, cuts, deformation, or debris. Clean external surfaces only according to approved practices. Expected outcome: The sealing surface is clean and appears properly seated. A damaged or displaced seal requires service rather than continued use.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Latch Alignment
steps.instructions: Check the externally visible latch, striker, hinge, or closure hardware for looseness, bending, or obvious misalignment. Do not adjust protected mechanical alignment unless authorized by manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: External closure hardware appears intact and aligned.

steps.title: 6. Verify Chamber Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm the chamber is not overfilled and that residual liquid, pressure, or an unfinished cycle is not preventing release. Do not attempt to force open a closure that may be held by an active safety interlock. Expected outcome: The system is in a safe state that should permit normal opening or closing.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Normal Control Sequence
steps.instructions: Use the standard operator controls to command lock, unlock, start, cancel, or reset only as normally permitted. Avoid repeated cycling of the mechanism if it binds or makes abnormal noise. Expected outcome: The closure responds normally and the system correctly recognizes its state.

steps.title: 8. Observe for Leakage During a Safe Test
steps.instructions: If the door or lid now closes normally, perform an appropriate unloaded test and inspect externally for leakage. Stop the test immediately if significant leakage appears. Expected outcome: The closure remains secure and no abnormal leakage is present. If successful, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 9. Check for Intermittent Recognition
steps.instructions: If the door physically closes but the system intermittently reports it open or unlocked, document whether gentle normal movement changes the indication. Do not bypass the switch or sensor. Expected outcome: An intermittent closure-recognition problem is identified for service escalation.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Closure Is Unreliable
steps.instructions: A cleaner with a door or lid that cannot consistently close, lock, release, or seal must not remain in processing service. Expected outcome: The unsafe closure condition is isolated and routed for repair.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the CaviWave Pro lid would not close completely and the cycle would not start.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an instrument basket positioned against the lid closure area.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned the basket, verified normal lid closure and recognition, completed an unloaded functional cycle, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Will not close, lock, unlock, or seal
Presence of trapped instruments or basket interference
Whether the system recognizes open/closed status
Whether the problem occurs loaded and unloaded

title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - Chamber Will Not Fill, Drain, or Reach Level
description: Use this guide for absent, slow, excessive, or incomplete filling and draining, or when the chamber cannot establish its normal operating level.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Continuity
steps.instructions: Stop using the cleaner if it cannot establish or remove the required chamber liquid level. An incomplete fill or drain can invalidate cleaning performance. Move instrument processing to a verified alternative. Expected outcome: No instruments depend on a cycle with uncertain liquid level or drainage.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Fluid Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the chamber does not fill at all, fills slowly, overfills, stops below the expected level, will not drain, or leaves an abnormal amount of residual water. Observe the phase in which the problem occurs. Expected outcome: The issue is categorized as a supply, fill, level, or drain problem.

steps.title: 3. Verify Incoming Water Availability
steps.instructions: Confirm required facility water service is available and accessible supply valves are open. Look for kinked, crushed, disconnected, or leaking external supply hoses. Expected outcome: Adequate external water supply is available. If restoring a closed or restricted supply corrects filling, verify a full cycle and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Inlet Screens or Accessible Strainers if User-Serviceable
steps.instructions: Where accessible without disassembly and allowed by normal maintenance practice, inspect externally serviceable strainers or screens for obvious debris. Do not disassemble internal valves or plumbing manifolds. Expected outcome: Accessible supply paths are unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Check the Drain Path
steps.instructions: Inspect visible drain hoses and facility drain connections for kinks, blockage, poor routing, backing-up water, or a facility drain problem. Expected outcome: The drain path is open and properly routed. If correcting an external drain restriction restores normal draining, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Chamber for Obstruction
steps.instructions: Check the chamber and accessible drain opening for labels, packaging debris, dropped items, excessive soil, or other visible material that could interfere with draining or level sensing. Expected outcome: The chamber and accessible drain area are free of obstruction.

steps.title: 7. Verify the Unit Is Properly Positioned
steps.instructions: Check that the cleaner has not been moved, tilted, or installed in a way that could affect drainage or fluid-level behavior. Do not alter installation leveling without appropriate authorization. Expected outcome: The unit appears correctly positioned and stable.

steps.title: 8. Observe Fill and Drain Behavior During an Unloaded Test
steps.instructions: Run an appropriate unloaded test cycle and observe the chamber through normal external means. Watch for water entering, stopping, draining, backing up, or leaking externally. Expected outcome: The chamber fills and drains in a controlled manner. If normal operation is restored, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Stop if Overfilling or Leakage Occurs
steps.instructions: If the unit continues filling excessively, spills water, or cannot stop at the intended level, terminate operation using normal controls and isolate the unit. Expected outcome: Further leakage or flooding is prevented.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Level Problems
steps.instructions: If water supply and drainage are good but level control remains abnormal, remove the unit from service. Expected outcome: The cleaner is routed for evaluation of internal fill, drain, or level-control functions.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the CaviWave Pro filled slowly and aborted before reaching the required operating level.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a kink in the external incoming water hose restricting flow to the cleaner.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the hose routing, verified normal filling and draining during an unloaded cycle, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: No fill, slow fill, overfill, or incomplete fill
No drain, slow drain, or residual water
Whether the unit was recently moved

title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - Temperature or Pressure Will Not Reach Setpoint
description: Use this guide when the cleaner cannot achieve or maintain its required temperature or reports an abnormal pressure-related process condition.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Integrity
steps.instructions: Do not consider a cycle acceptable if the cleaner cannot achieve the required process conditions. Remove affected loads from release and reprocess them according to departmental procedure. Expected outcome: No instruments are released from a cycle with unverified process conditions.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem is slow heating, no heating, unstable temperature, failure to reach a displayed target, or a pressure-related indication during filling, circulation, or another process phase. Record the displayed value and message without inventing expected specifications. Expected outcome: The affected process variable and cycle phase are clearly documented.

steps.title: 3. Verify Proper Chamber Fill
steps.instructions: Confirm that the unit is filling and maintaining a normal visible operating level. Heating and process control may be affected by inadequate water volume or an abnormal fill condition. Expected outcome: Fluid level appears normal. If the level is abnormal, troubleshoot the fill condition before continuing.

steps.title: 4. Check Facility Utilities
steps.instructions: Verify that required facility water and other applicable utilities are available and that external valves are open. Look for recent building outages, maintenance, unusually cold incoming water, or utility interruptions that correlate with the problem. Expected outcome: Required external utilities are available and stable.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Chamber and Load
steps.instructions: Confirm the chamber is not overloaded and that instruments are arranged according to normal departmental workflow. Excessive load, unusual load mass, or improper placement may affect cycle performance. Expected outcome: The load is reasonable and not obstructing normal process operation.

steps.title: 6. Verify Operator-Accessible Cycle Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended cleaning cycle was selected and that no user-adjustable setting was unintentionally changed. Do not alter protected temperature, calibration, or service settings. Expected outcome: The unit is operating with the intended authorized cycle configuration.

steps.title: 7. Inspect for Excessive Heat Loss or Leakage
steps.instructions: Check the lid or door for proper closure and inspect externally for significant leakage, abnormal steam or vapor release, or other evidence that the system is not retaining process conditions. Expected outcome: The chamber is properly closed and no abnormal external leakage is present.

steps.title: 8. Run an Appropriate Unloaded Functional Test
steps.instructions: If safe, run a test cycle and observe whether the displayed process value rises and stabilizes normally. Do not use an independent measurement to recalibrate the unit unless following an approved calibration procedure. Expected outcome: The unit reaches its normal cycle condition and completes successfully. If so, troubleshooting can stop after documentation.

steps.title: 9. Stop for Overtemperature or Unstable Control
steps.instructions: If the temperature rises abnormally, fluctuates significantly, or the system displays an overtemperature condition, discontinue operation. Expected outcome: Equipment with unreliable thermal control is removed from processing service.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Process-Control Failure
steps.instructions: If fluid level, utilities, loading, closure, and normal settings are correct but the unit still cannot establish the required process condition, remove it from service. Expected outcome: Service-level evaluation is initiated rather than attempting internal heater, sensor, or control repair at the equipment location.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the CaviWave Pro was taking unusually long to reach its normal operating temperature.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the chamber was not reaching a normal fill level because the incoming water supply was restricted.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the external water restriction, completed an unloaded cycle with normal filling and temperature progression, and returned the unit to service.

title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - Detergent, Chemistry, or Steam Delivery Fails
description: Use this guide when expected cleaning chemistry or another required process medium is not being delivered correctly during the cleaning cycle.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Integrity
steps.instructions: Do not release instruments from a cycle if required cleaning chemistry was absent, uncertain, or delivered incorrectly. Move the affected load to a verified reprocessing method. Expected outcome: Instruments are not considered cleaned based on an incomplete chemistry-delivery process.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What Failed to Deliver
steps.instructions: Determine what staff observed: empty chemistry container, no visible uptake, repeated low-chemistry indication, unchanged container level, disconnected tubing, or a cycle stopping during the dosing phase. Do not assume an internal pump failure before checking the supply path. Expected outcome: The delivery problem is described precisely.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Chemistry Is Available
steps.instructions: Confirm an approved chemistry container is installed and contains adequate product. Check that the product has not been substituted with an incorrect container or incompatible chemistry. Expected outcome: Correct chemistry is available to the unit.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Pickup Tubing and Connections
steps.instructions: Trace the accessible chemistry tubing from the container to the cleaner. Look for kinks, loose fittings, cracked tubing, disconnected pickup lines, tubing pinched behind the unit, or a pickup tube not reaching the product. Expected outcome: The external chemistry path is intact and properly positioned. If correcting a loose or kinked line restores delivery, verify operation and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Check for Air Entry or Loss of Prime
steps.instructions: Look for large visible air gaps in transparent tubing where applicable or evidence that the container was recently replaced and the system has not resumed normal uptake. Use only normal operator-accessible priming or setup functions when specifically authorized for the device. Expected outcome: The external supply line is filled or positioned for normal uptake without unauthorized service intervention.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Container Cap and Venting Arrangement
steps.instructions: Verify that the chemistry container, cap, adapter, or pickup assembly is installed as intended and is not cross-threaded, loose, or obviously obstructed. Expected outcome: The supply container interfaces correctly with the cleaner.

steps.title: 7. Verify Cycle and User-Accessible Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm the selected cycle is one that normally uses the expected chemistry and that no accessible setting has unintentionally changed. Do not alter dosing calibration or protected concentration settings. Expected outcome: The proper cycle is selected with authorized settings.

steps.title: 8. Observe an Unloaded Functional Cycle
steps.instructions: If safe and permitted, run an appropriate unloaded test and observe the accessible chemistry supply for evidence of normal uptake. Do not rely solely on visual movement if the manufacturer requires a specific verification method. Expected outcome: Chemistry delivery resumes and the cycle completes normally. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Stop for Leaks or Uncontrolled Chemical Release
steps.instructions: If chemistry leaks externally, tubing has failed, or the dosing system behaves unpredictably, discontinue use and follow applicable chemical-safety procedures. Expected outcome: Personnel exposure and equipment damage are prevented.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Delivery Failure
steps.instructions: If the chemistry source and external tubing are correct but delivery remains absent or inconsistent, remove the unit from service. Expected outcome: Internal dosing or control functions are evaluated by qualified service personnel.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the CaviWave Pro was not drawing detergent during the cleaning cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the detergent pickup tubing kinked behind the chemistry container.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the tubing routing, verified detergent uptake during an unloaded functional cycle, and returned the cleaner to service.

title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - Leak Test or Process Challenge Test Fails
description: Use this guide when a required cleaning-performance, cavitation, process-challenge, or related verification test does not produce the expected result.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Integrity
steps.instructions: Do not continue normal instrument processing based on a failed cleaning-performance or process-challenge result. Follow department policy for loads processed since the last acceptable verification if applicable. Expected outcome: Potentially ineffective cleaning is contained and not assumed acceptable.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Test That Failed
steps.instructions: Identify the exact test or challenge used, how it was performed, and what constituted the reported failure. Do not substitute one test method for another unless permitted by the applicable procedure. Expected outcome: The failed verification method and observed result are clearly documented.

steps.title: 3. Confirm the Test Material Was Valid
steps.instructions: Inspect the test device, indicator, foil, challenge item, or other consumable used for damage, expiration where applicable, incorrect storage, or prior use. Expected outcome: A valid test material was used. If the original test item was compromised, repeat the test using a valid item.

steps.title: 4. Verify Correct Test Placement
steps.instructions: Confirm the challenge device was placed in the chamber according to the applicable test procedure and was not shielded by a basket, instrument load, or other object. Expected outcome: Test placement does not invalidate the result.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Chamber Fill and Water Condition
steps.instructions: Verify the chamber fills normally and that the water condition is appropriate for the required process. Check for abnormal fluid level, excessive debris, or an overdue solution change according to department workflow. Expected outcome: The test is being performed in normal chamber conditions.

steps.title: 6. Verify Chemistry and Cycle Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct approved chemistry and intended cycle are being used when the test procedure requires them. Do not change concentrations or protected settings merely to make the test pass. Expected outcome: Test conditions match the normal approved cleaning process.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Loading Accessories
steps.instructions: Check racks, baskets, trays, and chamber accessories for incorrect placement, damage, or unusual configurations that could interfere with fluid circulation or ultrasonic energy distribution. Expected outcome: Chamber accessories are correctly positioned and do not obstruct the test area.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Test Once Under Correct Conditions
steps.instructions: Using a new or otherwise valid challenge item, repeat the test under documented correct conditions. Avoid repeatedly testing a failing unit without investigating the cause. Expected outcome: The test passes. If it does, document the corrected external cause and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Compare With an Unloaded Cycle
steps.instructions: If appropriate to the verification method, determine whether the failure persists with the chamber otherwise unloaded. Expected outcome: A persistent failure independent of load configuration is identified for escalation.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service After a Confirmed Repeat Failure
steps.instructions: If the correctly performed test fails again, remove the cleaner from processing use. Do not adjust ultrasonic output, calibration, transducers, or protected service parameters without approved service documentation. Expected outcome: The unit is withheld from service until cleaning performance can be restored and verified.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that the CaviWave Pro failed the department's ultrasonic cleaning-performance challenge.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the challenge device had been positioned beneath an incorrectly seated basket that shielded the test location.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the basket and challenge-device placement, repeated the approved test successfully, and returned the cleaner to service.

title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - Load Remains Wet or Cleaning Results Are Poor
description: Use this guide when instruments emerge visibly soiled, residue remains, cleaning effectiveness is poor, or retained moisture is considered abnormal for the workflow.

steps.title: 1. Protect Processing Quality
steps.instructions: Do not release instruments that remain visibly soiled or otherwise fail the department's cleaning acceptance criteria. Reprocess affected instruments using a verified method. Expected outcome: Inadequately cleaned instruments do not progress further in the reprocessing workflow.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Quality Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the concern is visible soil, residue, retained debris in joints or lumens, spotting, excessive remaining water, or generally inconsistent cleaning results. Identify whether the problem affects every load or only specific instruments. Expected outcome: The complaint is narrowed to a repeatable quality issue.

steps.title: 3. Review Load Arrangement
steps.instructions: Inspect how instruments are being placed into baskets or racks. Look for overloading, stacked items, closed hinged instruments, nested surfaces, or positioning that prevents fluid contact. Expected outcome: Instruments are arranged so cleaning solution can contact the required surfaces. If correcting loading restores cleaning quality, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check for Inappropriate Instrument Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm that the instruments being placed in the ultrasonic cleaner are suitable for the process and any required accessories are being used. Do not attempt to clean devices in a manner contrary to their reprocessing requirements. Expected outcome: The load is appropriate for ultrasonic cleaning.

steps.title: 5. Verify Chemistry Condition
steps.instructions: Check that the correct approved chemistry is connected, available, and being delivered. Look for incorrect product, empty container, obvious dilution error introduced externally, or tubing problems. Expected outcome: The cleaning solution is appropriate and available to the process.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Chamber Solution Condition
steps.instructions: Check for excessive visible debris, contamination, or solution conditions inconsistent with the department's established workflow. Expected outcome: The chamber solution is suitable for continued processing or is changed according to approved workflow.

steps.title: 7. Verify Chamber Fill and Cycle Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit reaches a normal operating liquid level and that staff are selecting the intended cleaning cycle. Expected outcome: The load receives the intended cycle under normal fill conditions.

steps.title: 8. Inspect Baskets and Accessories
steps.instructions: Check baskets, racks, holders, and other accessories for damage, blockage, incorrect installation, or accumulated debris that could interfere with cleaning action. Expected outcome: Accessories are clean, intact, and properly positioned.

steps.title: 9. Perform an Approved Cleaning-Performance Test
steps.instructions: If poor cleaning persists, perform the department's approved process-challenge or ultrasonic-performance verification. Do not infer ultrasonic performance solely from audible sound. Expected outcome: The unit passes the applicable verification. If the test passes, investigate workflow or load-specific factors before assuming equipment failure.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Confirmed Performance Failure
steps.instructions: If correct loading, chemistry, fluid conditions, cycle selection, and accessories are verified but cleaning remains inadequate or the performance test fails, remove the unit from service. Expected outcome: The cleaner is withheld from use pending service evaluation and successful performance verification.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that instruments were coming out of the CaviWave Pro with visible debris remaining between hinged surfaces.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the basket was overloaded and several hinged instruments were closed during processing.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the loading arrangement, repeated the cleaning process with instruments properly positioned, verified acceptable cleaning results, and returned the unit to normal use.

title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - Printer, Cycle Record, or Tracking Interface Fails
description: Use this guide when cycle documentation, printed records, data transfer, or an instrument-tracking interface is missing, incomplete, or unavailable.

steps.title: 1. Protect Documentation and Processing Traceability
steps.instructions: Determine whether department policy permits processing when electronic or printed cycle documentation is unavailable. If traceability cannot be maintained by an approved alternate method, stop affected processing until documentation is restored. Expected outcome: Required cycle records and instrument traceability are preserved.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What Function Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue affects printing, electronic record storage, network transfer, barcode or tracking integration, or all documentation functions. Confirm whether the cleaner itself still completes cycles normally. Expected outcome: A documentation problem is separated from a cleaning-process problem.

steps.title: 3. Check Printer Supplies and Physical Condition
steps.instructions: If a printer is involved, verify that paper or other normal consumables are present and correctly installed. Inspect accessible covers, feed paths, and connectors for obvious obstruction or damage. Expected outcome: The printer has required consumables and no simple mechanical obstruction.

steps.title: 4. Verify External Data Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible Ethernet, USB, serial, or other communication cables associated with the tracking interface. Check for loose connectors, damaged latches, pinched cables, or recent equipment movement. Expected outcome: Required data cables are securely connected and physically intact.

steps.title: 5. Check Link and Status Indicators
steps.instructions: Observe any normal network or peripheral status indicators available without entering restricted settings. A missing link indication may suggest a cable, wall jack, switch-port, or network problem. Expected outcome: Expected communication indicators are present or the failure is narrowed to the infrastructure path.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Correct User-Accessible Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify the intended destination, printer selection, or tracking workflow using only normal user-accessible settings. Do not change IP addressing, protected interface mappings, or service-level configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The correct destination or workflow is selected.

steps.title: 7. Test the Peripheral Independently When Practical
steps.instructions: Where possible, verify the printer, cable, wall port, scanner, or tracking workstation using a known-good comparison without altering the cleaner's protected configuration. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the external peripheral, infrastructure, or cleaner interface.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If processing is not active, restart the cleaner and any external interface device through normal shutdown procedures. Do not repeatedly cycle power during active data transfer. Expected outcome: Communication and cycle-record functions recover. If they do, verify a new test record and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Verify Record Creation
steps.instructions: Run an appropriate test or review a newly completed cycle to verify that the cycle record is stored, printed, or transferred as intended. Expected outcome: A complete record is produced and available at the intended destination.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Interface Failure
steps.instructions: If the external cables, peripherals, and basic configuration are correct but the interface remains unavailable, escalate to the appropriate Clinical Engineering, IT, tracking-system, or manufacturer support team. Expected outcome: The cleaner remains appropriately restricted if required documentation cannot be maintained.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported that completed CaviWave Pro cycles were no longer appearing in the instrument-tracking system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network cable disconnected from the cleaner after the unit had been moved.
CCR.Resolution: Reconnected the network cable, verified communication and successful transfer of a new cycle record, and returned the system to normal use.

Recent equipment movement or network work

title: Crest Ultrasonics CaviWave Pro Ultrasonic Cleaner - Overtemperature, Leak, or Water-on-Floor Condition Occurs
description: Use this guide for abnormal heat, fluid leakage, overflowing, repeated overtemperature conditions, or water found beneath or around the cleaner.

steps.title: 1. Make the Area Safe Immediately
steps.instructions: Stop the cleaning process using normal controls when safe to do so. Keep personnel away from hot liquid, chemistry, wet floors, and electrical hazards. If water is near energized electrical equipment, follow facility electrical-safety procedures rather than reaching into the affected area. Expected outcome: Immediate personnel and electrical hazards are controlled.

steps.title: 2. Remove the Cleaner From Processing Use
steps.instructions: Do not continue operating the unit to "see if it leaks again" while instruments depend on it. Move processing to another verified method or cleaner. Expected outcome: A potentially unsafe unit is no longer part of the active instrument-processing workflow.

steps.title: 3. Identify the Source Without Disassembly
steps.instructions: Inspect externally for the highest or first visible point of moisture. Check the chamber rim, lid or door seal area, supply hoses, drain hose, chemistry tubing, external fittings, and surrounding facility plumbing. Do not remove panels merely to follow a leak internally. Expected outcome: The leak is identified as external, facility-related, or internal/unresolved.

steps.title: 4. Check for Chamber Overfill
steps.instructions: Determine whether water escaped because the chamber filled above its normal operating level. If the unit continues filling unexpectedly, stop operation and isolate the water supply when this can be done safely and according to facility procedure. Expected outcome: Uncontrolled filling is stopped and the unit remains out of service.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Supply and Drain Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible hoses and fittings for looseness, disconnection, cracks, kinks, or poor drain routing. Also determine whether the facility drain is backing up and making the cleaner appear to leak. Expected outcome: External plumbing defects are identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Lid or Door Seal Area
steps.instructions: Look for debris, misplaced baskets, damaged sealing surfaces, or an obstruction that could allow water to escape during operation. Expected outcome: The closure area is clean and unobstructed. A damaged seal or mechanical closure fault requires service.

steps.title: 7. Evaluate an Overtemperature Complaint
steps.instructions: If the concern is heat rather than visible leakage, document whether the cleaner displayed an overtemperature message, produced unusual heat externally, emitted an odor, or shut itself down. Do not restart a unit with signs of overheating, burnt odor, smoke, or melted components. Expected outcome: Potential thermal damage is recognized and the equipment remains isolated when necessary.

steps.title: 8. Dry and Inspect the Surrounding Area
steps.instructions: Once power and water hazards are controlled, ensure the floor and surrounding work area are made safe according to facility procedure. Check whether the moisture may have originated from adjacent plumbing or another nearby device. Expected outcome: The environmental source is distinguished from a confirmed cleaner leak.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Test Only After a Simple External Correction
steps.instructions: If the cause was clearly external and safely corrected, such as a loose accessible drain connection, perform an unloaded test while continuously observing the unit. Stop immediately if leakage, excessive temperature, abnormal smell, or uncontrolled filling recurs. Expected outcome: No further leak or thermal abnormality occurs. If the test completes normally, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service for Any Unresolved Leak or Thermal Fault
steps.instructions: If the source cannot be confidently identified and corrected externally, or the condition repeats, do not continue testing. Expected outcome: The unit is labeled and escalated before additional water or heat damage occurs.

CCR.Complaint: Sterile Processing reported water collecting on the floor beside the CaviWave Pro during operation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external drain hose partially disconnected from its facility drain connection.
CCR.Resolution: Secured the drain connection, dried the area, completed an unloaded cycle with no further leakage, and returned the cleaner to service.
